a 10-kV DMOSFET design that is stable at low temperature and exhibits low leakage current is possible by a combination of epitaxial regrowth and a N20-based oxide.
the use of a thin epitaxy on p-wells in combination with N20-based gate oxides allows 4H-Sic power MOSFETs with a stable subthreshold behavior over the entire temperature range of interest.
the epitaxial regrowth process and N20-based gate oxide process enable stable subthreshold behavior of 10-kV SiC DMOSFETS over a wide range of temperatures.

the development of 10-kV large-area DMOSFET devices that can operate with a stable subthreshold leakage current independent of temperature, which is essential for the implementation in future high-voltage power modules.
the development of 10-kV SiC DMOSFETS with a low leakage normally off subthreshold behavior.
the development of high-voltage 4H-Sic DMOSFET technology for high-voltage power switching applications, with the goal of providing low leakage and high current handling.

the 4H-Silicon carbide DMOSFET has now reached the level where it can be used in a large variety of applications.

the presented device design, fabrication and characterization results are a significant contribution towards the realization of high-voltage 4H-SIC DMOSFET devices that are capable of operating in the 100-200degC temperature range.
the epitaxial regrowth and N20 oxidation processes have been shown to provide a stable subthreshold behavior for 10-kV DMOSFET structures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have demonstrated the possibility to achieve a stable low-leak-age subthreshold characteristic for 10-kV SiC DMOSFETS, and that the design space of SiC DMOS structures can be explored using numerical modeling and verified with experimental results.
a stable subthreshold characteristic is achieved by an epitaxial regrowth process in conjunction with a low thermal budget oxidation process.
we developed a 4H-SIC DMOSFET that has a low-leakage subthreshold characteristic at low temperatures and is able to withstand high temperatures and high voltages.
The main takeaway from our work is that

epitaxial regrowth is an effective way to achieve a stable subthreshold behavior in 4H-SIc DMOSFET devices at high temperatures, while the gate oxide and epitaxial regrown layer thickness can be used to optimize the device performance.
the use of epitaxial regrowth and N20-based gate oxides enables a normally off 4H-Sic DMOSFET to maintain stable subthreshold leakage current over a wide temperature range.
the epitaxial regrowth of thin epitaxial layers on already implanted regions is an efficient and cost-effective way to reduce the subthreshold leakage current in 4H-Sic power devices.
